newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tostem plans over 60 bln yen capital investment.
newsitem.headline: Tostem plans over 60 bln yen capital investment.

text.p: Housing and interior materials maker Tostem Corp said on Thursday that it expected its capital investment in the year from April 1997 to exceed 60 billion yen.
Its 1996/97 capital spending is estimated at little less than 60 billion yen, a company spokesman said.
Of the capital investment planned for 1997/98, 35 billion to 40 billion yen will be spent in building plants for its housing and interior materials division, a Tostem official said.

Regarding the planned increase in Japan's consumption tax on April 1, the Tostem spokesman said that the company expected housing starts in 1997/98 to fall from the current year but this would not damage Tostem's earnings.
"We can cope with an expected decline in housing starts and it will not affect our earnings," he said.
He said the expected decline will be offset by an increase in construction during the current fiscal year as consumers rush to buy homes ahead of the tax hike.
He estimated that such buying would account for 10 percent to 15 percent of housing starts in 1996/97.
